_meta.purpose: Org campaign region/zone data. Regions are the operational theaters contracts can honestly be asked in (contract boards randomize within a planetary region); zones are the map nodes control is spent on.
_meta.sources: Author-curated from in-game observation and community references — verify availability and archetypes each patch.
_meta.model: Objectives are only ever generated at REGION level ('run 3 ground-combat contracts in the Crusader region'); completed work yields control % the org assigns to a ZONE in that region. A mission that happens to land on the target zone earns the on-site bonus (self-reported).
_meta.availability: Per region × type: 'common' rolls normally, 'rare' rolls with the scarcity bonus multiplier, 'none' is never generated. Region-level judgment calls — see _redline.
_meta.recipes: Each zone archetype declares the mix that fills its control meter. A category's contribution CAPS at its share — no single playstyle can take a zone alone. Buckets: combat (ship+ground), supply (hauling), industry (mining+salvage). Investigation feeds intel, not meters.
_meta.strataCodes: zone.strata = the body/location code in Strata's data (Mining repo). Map join: planets/map_positions. Ore-yield join: location_ores — only where the body is mineable (city planets and gas giants like ARC/CRU/PY5 have no ore table by design; stations never do). null = not in Strata data at all (e.g. Grim Hex).
_meta.onSite: zone.onSite = mission types that can actually occur AT that zone (gates the on-site bonus and push flavor). Absent = any type the region offers. Salvage is never on-site anywhere — it is Lagrange-random and credited system-wide as economy. Belts belong to their parent zone (work turns up in them sometimes); Lagrange stations are not zones.
_meta.investigationNote: region.investigationNote = what KIND of investigation work actually posts there, reported by players in game (quick missing-person cases vs long ASD/research investigations). Shown in the log modal so people know what to expect. Only fill this in from confirmed sightings — leave it out when unknown.
_meta.heroes: region.setPiece = a hero_adventures id — the region's one set-piece op, visible from day 1. Logged once per season (setpiece.done) for a control surge on the region's front + medals. Crusader=Siege of Orison, Hurston=Hathor, microTech=Yormandi, ArcCorp=Hyperion.
_meta.factionVoice: Antagonist factions are attribution flavor ONLY — say 'the Headhunters are likely behind this', never claim an in-game event that does not exist ('Headhunters are attacking Everus Harbor' will never be on a mission board). Objective text stays provider-accurate; the faction lives in the fiction line.
_redline: RESOLVED: Crusader planet itself hosts no combat or mining contracts — hauling only, plus the Siege of Orison set-piece. Region-level combat stays 'common' (carried by the moons); the zone's onSite list encodes the planet.
CONFIRM ground-combat 'rare' for the ArcCorp region (drafted from thin surface content on Lyria/Wala).
CONFIRM microTech region ground-combat 'common' (planet distribution centers carry it; the ice moons have little/none — hence their mining archetypes).
CONFIRM investigation 'common' across all four Stanton regions (needs nearby moons for the ASD line).
CONFIRM zone archetypes marked with 'confirm': bunker vs mining leanings per moon.
CONFIRM director faction skins — drafted from currently active groups only (Headhunters / Dead Saints; Bit Zeros as alternate).
Pyro and Nyx sections are v2 DRAFTS: region groupings follow the contract-hub clusters (Checkmate / Orbituary / Ruin Station anchors); availability drafted from the provider matrix.
Ore headlines rank crafting ores (Aslarite/Ouratite/Lindinium/Savrilium/Torite) just under Quantanium — redline the order if the market disagrees.
_meta.why: zone.why = the grounded reason to take it (real services / real geology); zone.ores = the body's notable ship-mining ores from the Strata tables, best first. Display-level truth — held-zone yields stay abstract until the economy layer lands.
_meta.powers: zone.power / region.regionPower = BOARD-ONLY effects granted while the zone is held (all zones for a regionPower). They change campaign math on this page — control gains, org materials, Director behavior, project costs — never anything in the real game. Org materials and ORG funds are campaign fiction earned by banking contracts.

rare.note: Scarce work is worth more control.

capital.name: Regional Capital
capital.blurb: The region's anchor — city, orbital station, the works. Taking it is the regional climax.

bunker-moon.name: Contested Moon
bunker-moon.blurb: Surface strongpoints and rough company. Won by force, held by supply.

mining-moon.name: Resource Moon
mining-moon.blurb: The prize is in the ground. Taken primarily by working it.

station.name: Station
station.blurb: A dock and its contract board. Whoever keeps it fed, owns it.

directorFaction.name: Headhunters
directorFaction.confirm: Alternate: Bit Zeros. Skins the opposition only — objectives stay provider-accurate.

hurston.name: Hurston
hurston.why: Lorville's rental terminals, Everus Harbor rearm, and the region's market — the operational heart of Hurston space.

power.name: Logistics Command
power.text: Hauling contracts count +25% more control — zones unlock faster.

aberdeen.name: Aberdeen
aberdeen.why: Cave networks worth a fortune in hand-mining — and Klescher's backyard. The rock below seals it.

power.name: Prison Watch
power.text: +1 intel to the HQ stores every day.

arial.name: Arial
arial.why: A working miner's moon — its ore table pays steady wages.

power.name: Refinery Queue
power.text: +1 metals to the HQ stores every day.

ita.name: Ita
ita.why: Quiet, remote, and mineral-rich — a supply line worth guarding.

magda.name: Magda
magda.why: Surface strongpoints and solid ore — a forward post over Lorville's shoulder.

power.name: Forward Garrison
power.text: Defend objectives in Hurston space need 2 contracts instead of 3.

regionPower.name: Hurston Secured
regionPower.text: Raids in Hurston space cost half control when they land.

crusader.name: Crusader
crusader.investigationNote: Missing-person cases post here — quick searches, not ASD delving.

crusader.name: Crusader
crusader.note: Gas giant — the planet itself posts hauling only. Its war is fought around the moons and settled at the Siege of Orison.
crusader.why: Orison's rentals and Seraphim Station's rearm keep the whole region flying — and the Siege of Orison decides its fate.

power.name: Orison Shipyards
power.text: Capital-class hulls from the org census can be commissioned here (projects).

cellin.name: Cellin
cellin.why: Bunker country. Whoever holds Cellin's strongpoints watches every approach to Crusader.

power.name: Early-Warning Net
power.text: Tomorrow's Director move is always shown — no intel needed.

daymar.name: Daymar
daymar.why: The classic proving ground — caves, outposts, and rock that pays. Holding Daymar is holding the region's crossroads.

power.name: Rally Point
power.text: Ground combat in Crusader space counts +50% more control.

yela.name: Yela
yela.note: Ice moon; its asteroid ring is part of the zone — work turns up there sometimes.
yela.why: The ring is the prize: belt mining on the org's doorstep, with Grim Hex traffic to watch.

power.name: Ring Claim
power.text: +1 metals/day, and industry in Crusader space counts +50% more control.

arccorp.name: ArcCorp
arccorp.note: City planet. Baijini Point carries no personal weapons or armor.
arccorp.why: Area18's rentals and market move the region's money; Baijini Point moves its freight (no personal gear there).

power.name: War Market
power.text: Swap org materials 1:1 in the treasury, and +2 supplies/day.

lyria.name: Lyria
lyria.why: One of Stanton's richest rocks — Quantanium runs shorten dramatically with Lyria secured.

power.name: Quantanium Claim
power.text: +1 metals and +100,000 ORG funds to the treasury every day — the good rock pays.

wala.name: Wala
wala.why: Gem country — ROC prospecting at scale, and a clean staging orbit over Area18.

power.name: Gem Exchange
power.text: +1 components to the HQ stores every day.

regionPower.name: ArcCorp Secured
regionPower.text: Every daily material income +1, and +50,000 ORG funds/day.

microtech.name: microTech
microtech.note: The ground fight lives here — the ice moons are quiet.
microtech.why: New Babbage rentals, Port Tressler rearm — and the distribution-center fight decides the surface.

power.name: The Fab Labs
power.text: Tech projects unlock — component work can be commissioned here.

calliope.name: Calliope
calliope.why: Ice-moon veins that feed the refineries — cold, quiet, profitable.

power.name: Cold Storage
power.text: Ignored relief calls no longer drain the HQ stores.

clio.name: Clio
clio.why: A gentle moon with honest ore — the safest industry posting in microTech space.

power.name: Listening Post
power.text: +1 intel to the HQ stores every day.

euterpe.name: Euterpe
euterpe.why: Frozen and forgotten — which is exactly what makes its deposits worth fencing off.

power.name: Ice Mines
power.text: +1 supplies to the HQ stores every day.

directorFaction.name: Headhunters
directorFaction.confirm: Pyro opposition skin — gang territory; could differ per region.

checkmate.name: Checkmate
checkmate.why: The lawful foothold in Pyro — contracts, rearm, and a bed this side of the gate.

monox.name: Monox
monox.why: Toxic ground and good rock — Pyro industry starts here.

orbituary.name: Orbituary
orbituary.why: Gang country's crossroads — whoever feeds it, owns the drift.

bloom.name: Bloom
bloom.why: Cold and bright — Bloom's ice fields pay, if the convoys survive.

ruinstation.name: Ruin Station
ruinstation.note: The far end of the system — longest haul.
ruinstation.why: The far anchor of the system — the longest haul, and the deepest foothold.

pyro4.name: Pyro IV
pyro4.why: Hard ground in a hard system — a fortress rock on the way to Terminus.

pyro5.name: Pyro V
pyro5.note: Gas giant with its own moon family — served by Gaslight.
pyro5.why: The gas giant's moon family funnels every route past Gaslight — position is the prize.

terminus.name: Terminus
terminus.note: Its belt is part of the zone — work turns up there sometimes.
terminus.why: The end of the line — its belt pays, and its position commands the outer system.

directorFaction.name: Dead Saints
directorFaction.confirm: Active in all three systems; the natural Nyx skin.

levski.name: Levski
levski.note: The only real port in the system. Missions post at the station boards — Levski, the gateways, the People Service stations; the Glaciem belt itself posts nothing (belt bounty work is taken from the boards).
levski.why: The only real port in Nyx — every contract in the system starts and ends here.
